{{Quote|Always and always the Duloks smirch our trails, play us their tricks, steal of our harvest. I have no trust for them.|translated=1|[[Warok/Legends|Warok]]|<ref name="TAOT" />}}
The '''Duloks''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. Unlike their distant relatives, the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], they were tall and lanky with long [[Ear/Legends|ears]], sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]], and [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] that ranged in [[Color/Legends|color]] from white to red. Duloks were covered in [[Hair/Legends|fur]] that came in dull shades of brown, gray, and green; the coat was of a uniform length except for tufts at the top of the head and the tip of the tail, as well as manes and beards in some individuals. Duloks typically wore little more than [[Bone/Legends|bone]] and feather decorations, and they burnt, carved, or painted symbols on their fur. Members of the species were often unkempt and infested with [[Insect/Legends|insects]]. The Duloks were capable of communicating with the Ewoks through that species' [[Language/Legends|language]], [[Ewokese/Legends|Ewokese]].

Duloks tended to live in [[Swamp/Legends|swampy]] regions on the Forest [[Moon/Legends|Moon]]. Their [[City/Legends|villages]] were made up of rotting [[Tree/Legends|logs]] and dark caverns, which they furnished with structures of bone, mud, skin, and wood. The species was divided into clans and tribes headed by a [[Chief/Legends|chief]] or [[King/Legends|king]]. The strongest Dulok present usually assumed this role and ruled by cowing the others into doing his bidding. [[Gender/Legends|Females]] were generally expected to do little more than bear [[Youngling/Legends|pups]], clean house, and cook food&mdash;including a [[Stew/Legends|stew]] called [[glock]] and prey such as [[Wistie/Legends|Wisties]] and [[Wokling/Legends|woklings]]. Duloks were religious, so some power fell to [[Shaman/Legends|shamans]] and other mystics. Some Dulok religious leaders had the ability to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] via [[totem magic]], and many of these succumbed to the temptations of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. The Duloks worshipped a [[Deity/Legends|deity]] known as the [[Night Spirit/Legends|Night Spirit]].

In contrast to the Ewoks, Duloks had a reputation as greedy, foul-tempered barbarians. Their culture was aggressive and warlike. They were rapacious hunters, and they made frequent raids on nearby settlements, armed with [[Spear/Legends|spears]], [[Axe/Legends|axes]], and other simple implements. Despite acknowledging kinship with the Ewoks, Dulok bands were particularly keen to conquer Ewok villages and thus posed a major threat to some Ewok tribes. A gang of Duloks under King [[Vulgarr/Legends|Vulgarr]] menaced the Ewok [[Bright Tree Village tribe|tribe]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] in the years of the Ewok [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo's]] youth, and another [[Gorneesh's tribe|tribe]], led by King [[Gorneesh/Legends|Gorneesh]], came into frequent conflict with those same Ewoks. Some Duloks had an uneasy alliance with [[Morag]], the [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] witch, to further their designs on Ewok holdings.

After Morag's [[Death/Legends|death]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Duloks of Gorneesh's band had to contend with a new threat: the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The Imperials demolished the [[Dulok Swamp]] and [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] many members of Gorneesh's tribe as part of their efforts to build a [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield bunker]] that could protect the Empire's [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] the moon. The Dulok captives were freed when the Bright Tree Ewoks intervened, but not before many of them were killed by a beast known as the [[Griagh]], which had been awakened by the Empire's destruction.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|They are scaly, bony lizards. They have big ears and small brains. My homeworld does not miss their kind when they die.|translated=1|Treek|<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Treek|Exotic Appetites}}</ref>}}
[[File:Dulok_from_SWE.png|thumb|left|175px|Duloks were tall and wiry.]]
Duloks were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] bipedal<ref name="EGAS" /> [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]]<ref name="mammal" /> adapted to the [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor's forest moon]]. Gangly beings,<ref name="EGAS" /> they stood from 1.2 to 1.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall. Sharp claws poked from their four-fingered [[Limb/Legends|hands]] and three-toed feet.<ref name="COE" /> Some groups<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided">{{GalaxiesAED}} depicts Duloks with no tails.</ref> had thin, expressive,<ref name="THV">{{Ewoks|The Haunted Village}}</ref> tufted tails.<ref name="COE" /> They were vertebrates, with a full [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]], including a long-faced skull, spine, clavicles, ribs, breastbone, arm and leg bones, pelvis, and tail bones.<ref name="SOE" /><ref name="ZG FB">{{Facebook|username=ZackGiallongo|url=ZackGiallongo/posts/694715113872084?comment_id=93709059&offset=0&total_comments=25|name=The Suitably Authenticated Zack Giallongo Page|date=October 31, 2013|nobackup=1}}</ref> Duloks had [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Blood/Legends|blood]].<ref name="SOE" /> They were excellent climbers.<ref>[[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] features several scenarios where Duloks climb quickly into [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]]. See, for example, "[[The Haunted Village]]," "[[Blue Harvest]]," and "[[Wicket's Wagon]]."</ref>

Members of the species were covered in dull-looking [[Hair/Legends|fur]]. Most commonly, this was green,<ref name="A Tale of Magic and Suspense">Only ''[[The Adventures of Teebo: A Tale of Magic and Suspense]]'' features non-green Duloks.</ref> but shades of blue-gray, gray,<ref name="TAOT" /> and brown<ref name="COE" /> were not unheard of, and many individuals displayed markings of a different color from the main coat. For example, most members of a [[Gorneesh's tribe|tribe]] that lived in a swamp near the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] had green body fur with gray [[Mouth/Legends|lips]], brown eyebrows, and a gray mask around the [[Eye/Legends|eyes]],<ref name="THV" /> while other members had brown [[Ear/Legends|ears]] and brows, and gray mustaches instead.<ref name="CCK" /> Most of a Dulok's fur was relatively uniform in length except for a longer shock atop the head.<ref name="TAOT" /> However, some Duloks sported tufts of longer hair, often of a different shade from the main coat. Examples included a mane around the shoulders, bushy beards, and unruly coiffures.<ref name="SOE" />

[[File:EwoksAndDuloksSizeComparison-BH.png|thumb|right|250px|Duloks were taller and lankier than Ewoks.]]
The tip of the [[Nose/Legends|nose]] and soles of the feet were the only naturally hairless portions of the Dulok anatomy;<ref name="TCOTT">{{Ewoks|The Cries of the Trees}}</ref> skin color varied from gray to light to dark pink<ref name="skin" /> and was often blotched by another tone.<ref name="TAOT" /> The species had two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], male and female.<ref name="TTJ">{{Ewoks|The Travelling Jindas}}</ref> The features of a Dulok's broad<ref name="CSWE I 214" /> face were screwed up into a constant scowl.<ref name="EGAS" /> A full set of [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] filled the mouth,<ref name="SOE" /> and the two sharp<ref name="CSDB" /> canines jutted from the prognathic lower jaw.<ref name="COE" />

Small, round eyes<ref name="CSWE I 214" /> squinted from below downcast brows.<ref name="THV" /> These orbs sometimes appeared a single shade of pink,<ref name="SWE 203" /> red,<ref name="CSWE I 214" /> yellow,<ref name="COE" /> orange,<ref name="SOE" /> or white,<ref name="CCK" /> but in some Duloks, the sclera was of a different color, such as yellow.<ref name="SOE" /> Dulok eyes were sensitive to bright light,<ref name="TTOL">{{Ewoks|The Tree of Light}}</ref> but in low-light conditions, their pupils narrowed to vertical slits.<ref name="SOE" /> The hairless Dulok nose was either black,<ref name="THV" /> gray,<ref name="SOE" /> or green. Two long, floppy ears protruded<ref name="COE" /> or drooped<ref name="GAL">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> from the sides of the head and tapered to either tufts of hair or pointy tips.<ref name="The Adventures of Teebo: A Tale of Magic and Suspense">Only ''[[The Adventures of Teebo: A Tale of Magic and Suspense]]'' features Duloks with non-tufted ears.</ref> The concave surface of each ear faced forward; in some Duloks it had a lighter color than the back of the ear.<ref name="SOE" />

While they groomed themselves using the materials available to them&mdash;such as a [[Unidentified multi-legged Endor creature|multi-legged creature]] used as a sponge<ref name="WW">{{Ewoks|Wicket's Wagon}}</ref> and stolen [[Ewok soap]]&mdash;<ref name="THV" /> Duloks had a hard time keeping clean. As a result, their fur often became mangy, unkempt,<ref name="TAOT" /> foul smelling,<ref name="SWCEL">{{InsiderCite|27|A Star Wars CELibration|A ''Star Wars'' CELibration}}</ref> and infested with parasitic [[Insect/Legends|insects]].<ref name="EGAS" /> Despite this paucity of hygiene, some Dulok ancients<ref name="SWGCG">[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> lived to a prodigious age: the Dulok [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] [[Umwak]] claimed that his uncle [[Murgoob]] had seen more than 600 seasons in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref>[[Umwak]]'s claim comes from "[[Wicket's Wagon]]." Depending on the meaning of the term ''season'' (1 [[Endor/Legends|Endorian]] year or 1/4 of an Endorian year), and using the figures from ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' this would make [[Murgoob]] either 655 or 163 [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]] old in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], when ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' places the events of the ''Ewoks'' cartoon series. ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' {{C|"Murgoob, the Great"}} gives Murgoob's age as "600 standard years."</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|How can we get the sun crystal, King Gorneesh?»<br />«Don't be foolish! We get it like the Duloks get anything . . . We ''steal'' it!|translated=1|A Dulok warrior asks King Gorneesh about Dulok strategy|<ref name="E13">[[Ewoks (1985) 13|''Ewoks'' (1985) 13]]</ref>}}
[[File:DulokVillage-THV.png|thumb|left|250px|Duloks usually settled their villages in swampy areas.]]
Although Ewoks and Duloks spoke mutually intelligible [[Language/Legends|dialects]]<ref name="language" /> and acknowledged a common heritage,<ref name="THV" /><ref name="WW" /> their interactions were seldom cordial. The Duloks hated and envied the Ewoks for enjoying what the Duloks saw as the better lifestyle in the bountiful forests.<ref name="COE" /> They reserved a litany of insults for their cousins: ''furball'',<ref name="ROTP">{{Ewoks|Rampage of the Phlogs}}</ref> ''fuzzy imp'',<ref name="TAOT" /> ''puffball'',<ref name="AGFS">{{Ewoks|A Gift for Shodu}}</ref> ''runt'',<ref name="ROTP" /> ''tree rat'',<ref name="A">{{Ewoks|Asha (episode)}}</ref> and&mdash;for the [[Wokling/Legends|woklings]]&mdash;''brat'' and ''brawling''.<ref name="ROTP" /> Duloks typically had short, one-word names; examples included Boogutt,<ref name="E13" /> Gorneesh,<ref name="THV" /> Murgoob,<ref name="WW" /> Ulgo,<ref name="TAOT" /> Umwak,<ref name="WW" /> Urgah,<ref name="THV" /> and Vulgarr.<ref name="TAOT" />

Meanwhile, most Ewoks saw Duloks as fierce, rival [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] at best;<ref name="EGAS" /> stupid, ill-mannered barbarians at worst.<ref name="COE" /><ref name="TAOT" /> ''Dulok brain'' was an Ewok insult,<ref name="WWb">[[Wicket's Wagon (book)|''Wicket's Wagon'' picture book]]</ref> and some Ewoks referred to their cousins as "scaly, bony [[Lizard/Legends|lizards]]" with big ears.<ref name="TOR" /> Although most Ewoks respected their cousins as fellow children of the Forest Moon, a host of Ewok taboos and folk beliefs surrounded the marsh-dwelling species,<ref name="TAOT" /> and few Ewoks mourned a Dulok's [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="TOR" /> Ewoks agreed on one point: Duloks were creatures best avoided.<ref name="TAOT" />

Duloks were rare; fewer than one percent of the Forest Moon's sentient inhabitants belonged to the species.<ref name="Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds">Although it does not mention the Duloks by name, ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' allocates only 1% of [[Endor/Legends|Endor's]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] population to species other than [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] and [[Yuzzum/Legends|Yuzzums]].</ref> These were divided into scattered clans<ref name="CSWE I 197">{{CSWECite|I|197|Donkuwah}}</ref> and tribes<ref name="COE" /> with names such as [[Donkuwah]], [[Korga]], and [[Pubam]].<ref name="SWGCG" /> Most groups eked out a living in Endor's marshlands, based in villages of caves, logs, and stumps,<ref name="COE" /> although some bands settled in dry areas,<ref name="GAL" /> rocky terrain<ref name="FPTP">''[[From Pencil to Pixel: The Art of Star Wars Galaxies]]''</ref> and subterranean complexes.<ref name="GAL" /> Families lived in caverns and mud huts<ref name="COE" /> surrounding the throne of the village ruler or an altar to Dulok gods. The throne of one Dulok king, [[Gorneesh/Legends|Gorneesh]], was made from a [[Tree/Legends|tree]] stump under piles of animal skins and bones.<ref name="EGAS" />

===Status===
{{Quote|Away with you! This is no rest perch for fuzzy imps. You trespass on the veranda of King Ulgo the Magnificent. Away! Away!|translated=1|Ulgo|<ref name="TAOT" />}}
[[File:Duloks-ShadowsOfEndor.png|thumb|right|200px|Colored markings and bone accoutrements were ways Duloks marked their individual status.]]
With the exception of utilitarian items such as cloth diapers for the [[Youngling/Legends|young]]<ref name="COE" /> and [[Eye patch/Legends|eye patches]] for the maimed,<ref name="THV" /> Duloks wore clothing to denote status rather than hide nudity or provide warmth.<ref name="COE" /> Common adornments included [[Piercing/Legends|earrings]], hair ornaments, and [[Necklace/Legends|necklaces]]<ref name="TCOTT" /> of [[Bone/Legends|bone]], feather,<ref name="COE" /> and horn;<ref name="TCOTT" /> and pieces of cloth wrapped about the body.<ref name="THV" /> Duloks often bound their ears and hair with cord; the hair of the head,<ref name="COE" /> jowls, and chin were sometimes adorned in this way.<ref name="SOE" /> Fur modifications&mdash;branding, painting, and shaving&mdash;signified status and tribal affiliation. Pigments for fur coloring included blue, yellow,<ref name="COE" /> and red.<ref name="THV" /> Similarly, a few Duloks carved tribal markings into their lower canines. Some members of the species wore [[Leather/Legends|leather]] pouches in which to carry their belongings.<ref name="COE" />

Bigger, more aggressive Duloks bullied and cowed their way up the social ladder.<ref>Examples of this bullying appear in such [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] episodes as "[[Rampage of the Phlogs]]," "[[The Travelling Jindas]]," and "[[The Tree of Light]]." Similarly, in ''[[The Adventures of Teebo: A Tale of Magic and Suspense]]'', [[Crooked Tail]] attempts to overthrow [[Vulgarr/Legends|Vulgarr]] by force.</ref> Individuals signified their place in the pecking order via jewelry, and symbols and designs on their teeth and fur.<ref name="COE" /> Dulok bullying was often verbal in nature; popular Dulok insults included ''churpo,''<ref name="BH">{{Ewoks|Blue Harvest}}</ref> ''dolt,''<ref name="CCK" /> and ''roothead.''<ref name="TTJ" /><ref name="WW" /><ref name="A" /><ref name="PB">{{Ewoks|Prow Beaten}}</ref><ref name="TTOL" /><ref name="AGFS" />

A [[Chief/Legends|chief]]<ref name="COE" /> or [[King/Legends|king]] headed each tribe. The position theoretically passed from [[Parent/Legends|father]] to son, but just as often, insurrection and regicide brought a new leader to power. The Dulok ruler [[Vulgarr/Legends|Vulgarr]] usurped the throne of another, [[Ulgo]], in this way, for example,<ref name="CSWE I 214" /> only to be the target of a coup attempt himself. Many Dulok kings kept a retinue of loyal [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] to shield them from such challenges.<ref>The coup against [[Vulgarr/Legends|Vulgarr]] is foiled by a Dulok loyal to the [[King/Legends|king]] in ''[[The Adventures of Teebo: A Tale of Magic and Suspense]]'', and [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] often accompany [[Gorneesh/Legends|Gorneesh]] in the [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] cartoon.</ref> Dulok rulers were prone to bombast, claiming, for instance, to be the king of ''all'' Duloks<ref name="TAOT" /><ref name="ROTP" /> and assuming epithets such as "the magnificent" and "the all powerful."<ref name="TAOT" /> Tribes with weak rulers were prone to constant in-fighting and arguments.<ref name="CCK" />

===Gender roles and family===
{{Quote|&hellip;rotten, miserable, monstrous, misbehaved brats!|translated=1|Queen Urgah, on her children with King Gorneesh|<ref name="TTJ" />}}
[[File:UmwakAndUrgahCeremony-NotS.png|thumb|left|250px|Shamans led ceremonies for the tribe.]]
Male Duloks served in various capacities. A medicine man or shaman advised the ruler<ref name="COE" /> and tended to the infirm.<ref name="CCK" /> Other Duloks acted as laborers,<ref name="SWGCG" /> [[Scout/Legends|scouts]],<ref name="toy">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Ewoks (toy line)|pack=Dulok Scout|link=Ewoks-Scout.asp}}</ref> and warriors. In some groups, high-ranking fighters took the title [[Dulok battlelord|''battlelord'']]. More seasoned members of the group were regarded as elders.<ref name="SWGCG" /> Duloks banished from their home became outcasts, forced into a life of solitary banditry and scavenging.<ref name="SWGTTE">[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Total Experience: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: The Total Experience'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> The Dulok Ulgo lived in this way after being deposed by Vulgarr.<ref name="TAOT" /> Dulok [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] populated the bottom of the social hierarchy.<ref name="COE" />

Duloks practiced monogamous [[Marriage/Legends|marriage]].<ref name="AGFS" /> The males could be doting husbands, spouting sweet nothings such as ''swampbunny'' to their beloved.<ref name="TTJ" /> Still, women enjoyed little status. They were primarily expected to bear and raise children<ref name="COE" /> and to take part in certain ceremonies,<ref name="NOTS">{{Ewoks|Night of the Stranger}}</ref> and even a Dulok [[Queen/Legends|queen]] could be assigned cooking duty.<ref name="ROTP" /><ref name="TTJ" /> Nevertheless, females were generally brighter than males. Some managed to claw their way into posts as scouts, a vocation for which they routinely outperformed their male counterparts, or as shamans or warriors.<ref name="COE" /> Women could exert influence behind the scenes; Queen [[Urgah]] sometimes browbeat King Gorneesh into acquiescing to her demands, for example.<ref name="TTJ" />

Dulok young were known as ''cubs'',<ref name="SWGCG" /> ''pups'',<ref name="TTOL" /> or ''brats''. Although caring for them was a chore often hoisted off to slaves,<ref name="TTJ" /> Duloks could be devoted parents. Gorneesh even formed a brief alliance with his enemies, the Ewoks of Bright Tree Village, when his son, [[Boogutt]], went missing.<ref name="E13" />

===Diet===
{{Quote|Behold the picnic of a lifetime. We'll have them fried and frizzled and braised and sizzled, stewed and simmered and grilled.|translated=1|Vulgarr, on woklings|<ref name="TAOT" />}}
[[File:XAndUrgah-RotP.png|thumb|right|250px|Glock was a Dulok dish.]]
Duloks were [[Diet/Legends|omnivores]].<ref name="TAOT" /> Many tribes sustained themselves by scavenging<ref name="SWGCG" /> for swamp fodder, such as berries<ref name="TAOT" /> and insects<ref name="AGFS" /> with meat supplementing such staples.<ref name="TAOT" /> [[Hunting/Legends|Hunting]] parties ranged throughout the swamp and into Endor's woods and plains.<ref name="EGC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref><ref name="RES">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> The Ewoks particularly disdained Dulok hunting practices, accusing their cousins of taking sadistic glee in the misery of their quarries, for trophy hunting,<ref name="A" /> and for valuing sport over sustenance.<ref name="TRG">''[[The Red Ghost: An Ewok Adventure]]''</ref> The Duloks' tastes in meat did not endear them to their relatives, either: they had no qualms about eating anything from [[Lantern bird/Legends|lantern birds]]&mdash;considered sacred to the Ewoks<ref name="TAOT" />&mdash;to sentient [[Wistie/Legends|Wisties]]<ref name="TCOTT" /> and even woklings.<ref name="TAOT" />

Although Duloks practiced small-scale [[Farm/Legends|agriculture]], they were fair-weather farmers at best. In some years, Dulok groups completely neglected to plant crops at all. Instead, a much more tempting target was to steal the harvest of nearby Ewoks.<ref name="BH" /> The species highly valued Ewok food,<ref name="DB EV">{{DB|location|ewokvillage|Ewok Village}}</ref> especially delicacies like [[Pie/Legends|pies]].<ref name="THV" /> One native Dulok dish was a thick stew called [[glock]].<ref name="ROTP" />

===Trade and technology===
{{Quote|Wah, hah! Vulgarr is a moon-headed fool. I once traded him two scrawny birds for this fine fur vest.|translated=1|Ulgo|<ref name="TAOT" />}}
[[File:Dulok_trap.png|thumb|left|220px|Duloks laid traps to capture slaves and game alike.]]
Dulok populations traded with one another and with groups of other species.<ref name="COE" /> Nevertheless, a reputation for duplicity kept many partners from fully trusting them.<ref name="EGAS" /> Dulok merchants traveled to the [[Gupin/Legends|Gupins']] volcanic home in the grasslands east of Endor's [[Great Forest]],<ref name="COE" /> and [[Travelling Jindas|Jindas]] played for the Duloks of Gorneesh's tribe, although they found their audience aggressive, boorish and lewd.<ref name="TTJ" /> The two-headed [[Gonster]] had dealings with members of the species,<ref name="TR">{{Ewoks|The Raich}}</ref> and [[Morag]], the [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] witch, traded the occasional favor and threats of [[Magic/Legends|magical]] retaliation for Dulok support in her schemes.<ref name="TCOTT" /> Slaves of many species, including Ewoks<ref name="ROTP" /> and other Duloks, were the main commodity of exchange between Dulok groups,<ref name="COE" /> although they also traded crafts, such as Ewok-fur clothing, and game, such as lantern birds.<ref name="TAOT" />

Duloks made stone-age tools and crafts from bone,<ref name="NOTS" /> fur, leather,<ref name="TAOT" /> rock, and wood.<ref name="COE" /> In addition to mundane items like tables,<ref name="CCK" /> they employed an arsenal of [[Spear/Legends|spears]], stone [[Axe/Legends|axes]]<ref name="TAOT" /> and [[Knife/Legends|knives]],<ref name="E13" /> wooden [[Club/Legends|clubs]],<ref name="TAOT" /> [[Catapult/Legends|catapults]],<ref name="PB" /> and [[Grappling hook/Legends|grappling hooks]]. Shamans often knew arcane formulae by which they could create things such as [[smoke powder]]<ref name="BH" /> and "[[Umwak's special glasses|special glasses]]" designed to show the way through confusing terrain.<ref name="TTOL" /> While Duloks did not employ [[Hang-glider/Legends|hang gliders]] to take to the air,<ref name="TAOT" /> they did build boats and battleships for use in river raids.<ref name="PB" />

Duloks often set traps and snares that incorporated cages,<ref name="A" /> nets,<ref name="AGFS" /> [[Rope/Legends|ropes]],<ref name="CCK" /> poles, and stones.<ref name="E10">[[Ewoks (1985) 10|''Ewoks'' (1985) 10]]</ref> These were used to stop intruders,<ref name="TAOT" /> trap game,<ref name="A" /> and capture slaves.<ref name="AGFS" /><ref name="PB" /> Captives were wheeled about in cage wagons cobbled together from sticks and skins until they could be eaten,<ref name="TAOT" /> ransomed,<ref name="CCK" /> or put to other use. Dulok clothing was made from woven cloth,<ref name="THV" /> skins, and furs&mdash;including that of Ewoks.<ref name="TAOT" /> Their medicine was sophisticated enough to treat severe wounds.<ref name="SOE" />

===Raiding and war===
{{Quote|Get 'em! Stomp 'em! Smash 'em!|translated=1|A Dulok battle cry|<ref name="WW" />}}
While they rarely showed the pluck and flair so often attributed to their forest cousins,<ref name="DB EV" /> Duloks excelled at fighting, raiding, and stealing.<ref name="EGAS" /> The dearth of resources in their swamp habitat gave then little choice,<ref name="COE" /> and a preference for idleness to backbreaking labor<ref name="DB EV" /> and their might-makes-right culture both added to the appeal of such behavior.<ref name="TRG" /> Some Dulok bands ranged several days from their home, basing themselves in camps while away.<ref name="TAOT" /> Ewok villages fielded scouts of their own to watch out for such bandits.<ref name="Official Star Wars Fact File 109">{{FactFile|109|EWO 9-12|Ewok Warriors}}</ref>

Scouts were tasked with finding choice targets and opportune times to strike.<ref name="WW" /> Still, Duloks preferred to avoid confrontation;<ref name="THVb">[[The Haunted Village (book)|''Haunted Village'']]</ref> much better to sneak into rival territory and steal undetected<ref name="DB EV" /><ref name="BH" /> or to hoodwink their targets to Dulok ends. The shaman Umwak, for example, often disguised himself to fool the Ewoks of Bright Tree Village,<ref name="CSWE III 280">{{CSWECite|III|280|Umwak}}</ref> and Vulgarr's band of Duloks used a giant, foot-shaped stone to make prints they later blamed on a large creature supposedly menacing the area.<ref name="TAOT" /> Dulok ruses sometimes hinged on bamboozling more naive marks like giant [[Phlog/Legends|Phlogs]] to unwittingly do their dirty work.<ref name="COE" />

[[File:Dulok.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A war dance sometimes preceded a raid.]]
When numbers were in their favor, however, Duloks grew bold. Their targets including [[Jinda/Legends|Jindas]]<ref name="COE" /> and [[Sanyassan/Legends|Sanyassan]] [[Sanyassan Marauders/Legends|Marauders]],<ref name="DB Yavid">{{DB|character|generalyavid|Yavid, General}}</ref> but they particularly found their diminutive Ewok brethren easier prey<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>&mdash;and Ewok food and handicrafts their most tempting prizes.<ref name="DB EV" /> Ewok lore told of Dulok raiders driving Ewoks away and taking over entire villages.<ref name="EGAS" /> Some Ewok tribes settled their villages in more inaccessible areas, such as in the middle of [[Water/Legends|lakes]], to avoid Dulok raiders.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 79">{{FactFile|79|END 9-10|Endor &ndash; Lake Dwellings}}</ref> Duloks themselves had to contend with the [[vroom]]-riding [[Pugs]].<ref name="PE">{{Ewoks|Party Ewok}}</ref>

A raid might have begun with a war dance around a village bonfire.<ref name="THV" /> Then the chief or king personally might have led the charge.<ref name="E13" /> If their target was an Ewok tree village, the raiders climbed straight up using vines<ref name="THV" /> or grappling hooks,<ref name="BH" /> or scaled nearby trees and swung in on vines.<ref name="NOTS" /> Dulok warriors attacked with whoops, hollers,<ref name="TAOT" /> and battle cries.<ref name="TTOL" /> They could be fierce combatants; even with more advanced weaponry, the Marauders only kept them at bay through the battle strategies of General [[Yavid]].<ref name="DB Yavid" /> Despite the threat they posed, Ewoks saw Duloks as fellow creatures of the forest and killed them only with reluctance.<ref name="TAOT" /> Some Ewoks, such as [[Graak]] of Bright Tree Village, became specialists in anti-Dulok tactics.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 109">{{FactFile|109|EWO 9-12|Ewok Warriors}}</ref>

Duloks followed victorious attacks with revelrous indulgence in their booty back at the village.<ref name="BH" /> Many Dulok raids failed due to poor planning, inept execution, or unforeseen complications.<ref name="THV" /><ref name="WW" /><ref name="TTJ" /> Others ended once the targets managed to rally reinforcements; even versus the smaller Ewoks, Duloks preferred flight to fight when outnumbered.<ref name="TAOT" /><ref name="TTOL" /><ref name="BH" /> Failed raiders could do little but bandage their wounded and plot their next incursion.<ref name="CCK" />

===Religion===
{{Quote|Soon, all Endor will be ruled by the Night Spirit and its most devoted fan: Me!|translated=1|Gorneesh|<ref name="TTOL" />}}
[[File:AshaDulok-SWG4.jpg|thumb|left|195px|Asha fends off Dulok poachers.]]
Duloks were superstitious creatures.<ref name="A" /><ref name="TAOT" /> According to their mythology, the woodland deities had forsaken them to their wretched swamps and allowed the hated Ewoks dominion over the forests.<ref name="COE" /> Duloks acknowledged the power of the natural entities sacred to the Ewoks, such as the [[Soul Tree]]s and [[Tree of Light]], but the Duloks desired to destroy, rather than worship, them.<ref name="WW" /><ref name="TTOL" /> They feared the Ewok [[Asha/Legends|Asha]], whom they considered a ferocious forest spirit,<ref name="SWGS4">{{Topps|set=2009 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 4|cardname=Night of the Red Ghost|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/75146/cid/6271136/2009-Topps-Star-Wars-Galaxy-4-21-Night-of-the-Red-Ghost}}</ref> and they believed the Ewoks to consort with foul [[Demon/Legends|demons]]; Gorneesh's tribe mistook the droid [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] for such an abomination<ref name="E10" /> in 3 ABY.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> Instead, the Duloks worshipped&mdash;and feared&mdash;a divinity known as the [[Night Spirit/Legends|Night Spirit]].<ref name="TTOL" /><ref name="NOTS" />

Those Duloks thought able to consult with spirits could obtain high rank. Most groups had a medicine man or shaman<ref name="COE" /> who led ceremonies. In one ritual performed by Umwak, the tribe gathered around a bonfire and played music while the shaman, in a headdress, danced with Queen Urgah, who held a stone.<ref name="NOTS" /> A group's shaman often became one of the ruler's most trusted advisers.<ref name="COE" /> In addition, some groups had an [[Dulok oracle|oracle]] thought to be able to predict the future,<ref name="SWE 203" /> [[Dulok adept|adepts]], and [[spiritmaster]]s.<ref name="SWGCG" /><ref name="SWGQRG">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided Quick Reference Guide]]''</ref> A large altar of wood, skins, and bones often occupied a prominent spot in a Dulok village.<ref name="EGAS" /> Mystics were distinguished by their regalia; the shaman Umwak carried a staff capped by a large skull,<ref name="ROTP" /> and the oracle Murgoob carried a knotted staff.<ref name="WW" />

Although such Duloks could simply fake supernatural abilities,<ref name="TCOTT" /> some sorcerers were indeed [[The Force/Legends|Force]] users. Still, they had to rely on [[Totem magic|totems]] and talismans to access the energy field. Such individuals were particularly prone to the temptations of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]],<ref name="COE" /> a propensity that earned them a reputation for dark magic from some Ewoks.<ref name="SOE" /> Nevertheless, a few Dulok shamans employed their gifts to better the lot of their fellow villagers&mdash;and were branded as oddballs for their efforts.<ref name="COE" />

==History==
===Evolution and Ewok rivalry===
{{Quote|I warred with a Dulok tribe in the Sagreb Swamps. They regretted challenging me. I claimed Dulok ears for my necklace!|translated=1|Treek|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Battle_at_the_Dulok_Meadow.png|thumb|right|185px|Chief Chirpa's Ewoks drove away King Vulgarr's Dulok bandits.]]
The Duloks evolved on the Forest Moon of Endor<ref name="CSDB" /> from a common ancestor with the Ewoks. Following their evolutionary split, the Ewoks took to Endor's vast woodlands, while the Duloks were relegated to the moon's sparse bogs<ref name="COE" /> and more desolate areas.<ref name="GAL" />

From former familiarity emerged fierce rivalry as Dulok groups harassed and bullied their Ewok neighbors.<ref name="EGAS" /> As early as [[3640 BBY]],<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> members of the two species warred with one another. For instance, around that [[Time/Legends|time]]&mdash;during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]&mdash;the Ewok [[Treek/Legends|Treek]] claimed to have bested the Duloks of the [[Sagreb Swamps]]; when she entered their territory, her story went, they targeted her for her skin&mdash;only to have Treek cut their ears off and string them onto a necklace.<ref name="TOR" />

Over years of outright war, other Duloks were more successful. The species developed into apt raiders: Ewok villages fell,<ref name="EGAS" /> and Ewok tribes were wiped out in the face of the taller species.<ref name="COE" /> Dulok bands developed combative relationships with neighboring groups of Ewoks. For example, the Pubam Duloks opposed the [[Gondula]] and [[Panshee]] Ewoks from the [[Dulok Village (south)|Dulok Village]].<ref name="SWGCG" />

One band of Duloks, headed by King Ulgo and, after a coup, King Vulgarr,<ref name="CSWE I 214" /> menaced the Ewoks of Bright Tree Village in the years of the Ewok [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo's]] youth. In one encounter, Vulgarr and his warriors tricked the Ewoks into believing that a monster had kidnapped the wokling [[Malani]]. When Chief [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]] and a troop of warriors set off to find the perpetrator, Vulgarr and his soldiers ransacked the undefended village and kidnapped its woklings. Only a combined assault by the returning Ewok warriors and a giant known as the [[Grudakk|Grundakk]] routed the invaders and freed the wokling slaves. The Ewok shaman [[Logray/Legends|Logray]] planted Vulgarr in the ground and declared that he would grow into a gnarled tree as a warning to other would-be Dulok brigands.<ref name="TAOT" />

==Duloks in the galaxy==
===Gorneesh's tribe===
{{Quote|We Duloks were all set to take over the forest when they brought out that cursed wagon and knocked us clear back into the swamps. How I'd love to get my hands on that thing! I'd teach those Ewoks a lesson!|translated=1|Murgoob|<ref name="WW" />}}
Gorneesh's tribe was a relatively large band<ref name="SWE 83">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' {{C|"Dulok"}}</ref> that lived in the [[Dulok Swamp]] just beyond the borders of [[Happy Grove/Legends|Happy Grove]].<ref name="TRG" /> Under the leadership of the hulking, one-eyed King Gorneesh, they proved a persistent pest to the Ewoks and schemed to steal their harvest, kidnap their woklings, and take over their village,<ref name="E10" /> with several hostile encounters in 3 ABY.<ref name="BTM" /> This harassment often manifested as simple raids, as when Gorneesh and his warriors stole Logray's [[shadowroot soap]], became invisible, and invaded Bright Tree Village.<ref name="THV" /> In another encounter, they tried to steal the Ewoks' [[sun crystal]] but accidentally destroyed it instead.<ref name="E13" />

Duloks of Gorneesh's tribe kidnapped Ewoks to do the tasks they despised, such as caring for their pups<ref name="TTJ" /> and cleaning their village.<ref name="ROTP" /> During one raid, they sneaked into Bright Tree Village while the Ewoks were preoccupied with their annual [[Halloween/Legends|Hallowe'en]] party. In an accident, the Ewok Chirpa fell into a sack and was carried away by the Duloks, who thought he was a sack of food. When they realized their mistake back at camp, they decided to hold him for ransom. A group of young Ewoks from the village entered the camp, and Chirpa took advantage of the commotion to escape his bonds and fight his way back to his village.<ref name="CCK" />

[[File:StealingTheBattleWagon-WW.png|thumb|left|250px|Duloks spy on the reconstruction of the Ewok battle wagon.]]
The two tribes fought a long [[Ewok–Dulok wars/Legends|war]]. In a decisive battle, the Duloks advanced on the Ewoks' Soul Trees with axes and tried to cut them down, but the Ewok [[Erpham Warrick]]'s [[Ewok battle wagon|battle wagon]] drove the raiders away.<ref name="WW" /><ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 1">{{FactFile|1|WIC 1-4|Wicket W. Warrick}}</ref> Three generations later, the Ewoks' sacred Tree of Light grew weak and needed renewal. Gorneesh and his band rushed to fell it before the Ewoks could perform the necessary ceremony, but in the ensuing battle, the Ewoks [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket W. Warrick]] and [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]] foiled the plot.<ref name="TTOL" />

The Duloks later managed to steal Erpham Warrick's reconstructed battle wagon and aimed it at the Soul Trees, but Wicket W. Warrick destroyed the war machine before it could reach the sacred grove.<ref name="WW" /> During another scheme, the Duloks stole a sacred fish carving from the Ewoks and used it for their own [[Dulok battleship|battleship]], but it was recovered by Wicket W. Warrick and his companions, who had been pressed into service as galley slaves.<ref name="PB" /> In one instance, Gorneesh capitalized on the long war by pretending to proffer a peace treaty.<ref name="D4">[[Droids (1986) 4|''Droids'' (1986) 4]]</ref> However, during the [[Chirpa–Gorneesh peace summit|Chirpa-Gorneesh peace summit]], he ordered his troops to cut the ropes holding up a bridge once the Ewok delegation started across.<ref name="E10" />

{{Unlicensedstart}}
Other schemes hatched by Gorneesh and company included trying to prevent the Ewoks from harvesting [[Berry/Legends|berries]],<ref name="PKB">{{StoryCite|story=Princess Kneesaa's Birthday|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 1}}</ref> setting snares and traps to capture Ewoks,<ref name="SitF">{{StoryCite|story=Snare in the Forest|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 4}}</ref><ref name="TTL">{{StoryCite|story=To Trap Latara|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 6}}</ref> attempting to steal an Ewok balloon,<ref name="TB">{{StoryCite|story=The Balloon|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 5}}</ref> and scheming to steal the Ewok shaman Logray's magical [[Staff of Logray|staff]].<ref name="LS">{{StoryCite|story=Logray's Staff|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 7}}</ref>
{{Unlicensedend}}

[[File:GorneeshBoogutt-E13.png|thumb|right|315px|Gorneesh and Boogutt participate in a raid]]
Members of the tribe, including Gorneesh's wife, Urgah,<ref name="WW" /> and son, Boogutt,<ref name="E13" /> participated in raids and schemes. The shaman, Umwak, represented the tribe in dealings with the witch Morag<ref name="TCOTT" /> and occasionally scouted with his [[Umwak's nephew|nephew]].<ref name="TTOL" /> The tribe often found itself relegated to the role of henchmen by other powerful Ewok enemies. For example, Morag once delivered a baby Phlog named [[Nahkee]] to the tribe and ordered them to watch over him; still, a group of young Ewoks freed the infant, and his enraged family terrorized the swamp-dwellers in revenge.<ref name="ROTP" /> Similarly, a being known as the [[Stranger]] frightened the Duloks into raiding Bright Tree Village; during the distraction, he stole the Ewoks' [[Sunstar/Legends|Sunstar-Shadowstone]].<ref name="NOTS" />

===Relations with the galaxy===
{{Quote|The "dark form" of the Ewoks, the Duloks are ill-proportioned cousins featuring fangs and large, pointed ears.|Corellian Security Force description of Duloks from the Imperial era|<ref name="CSDB" />}}
[[File:Clone_Wars_Dulok.jpg|thumb|left|215px|A Dulok on Coruscant]]
Over centuries, Endor's massive [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] shadow and cloak of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]-borne detritus crashed hundreds of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] on the Forest Moon. A few of these offworld crew and passengers survived and managed to eke out a living.<ref name="EATMS">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref> In this way, the Duloks came into contact with Gupins, Jindas, Phlogs,<ref name="COE" /> Sanyassans,<ref name="DB Yavid" /> Tulgah, and other species.<ref name="COE" /> Duloks struck up trade relations with some of these,<ref name="COE" /> fealty to others,<ref name="THV" /> and covetous designs on still more.<ref name="COE" /> Those few ships that managed to return to the [[Star/Legends|stars]] spread the [[Moon/Legends|moon's]] lifeforms beyond their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]],<ref name="COE" /> and at least one Dulok was present on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].<ref name="CW 21">{{CW|21}}</ref><ref name="21BBY">"[[Chapter 21 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|Chapter 21]]" of ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' depicts the [[Battle of Hypori/Legends|Battle of Hypori]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].</ref>

Still, Endor was far from [[The galaxy/Legends|the galactic]] [[Deep Core/Legends|core]] and only accessible through a long and difficult [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] journey.<ref name="DB Endor">{{DB|location|endor|Endor}}</ref> Although the Forest Moon&mdash;along with the rest of the [[Inner Zuma Region]]&mdash;ostensibly became part of the Galactic Republic in [[50 BBY/Legends|50 BBY]], it remained mostly unknown in the galaxy at large.<ref name="EATMS" /> The Duloks, as a relatively scarce species, were even more obscure. While [[Corellian Security Force]] intelligence knew of the species by [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] and included a brief description of them in their classified [[CorSec Database]],<ref name="CSDB" /> a report filed by Imperial scout [[Pfilbee Jhorn]] before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] either missed the Duloks completely or deemed them unworthy of mention. This report became the most well-read account of the Forest Moon's inhabitants for the eight years following the fall of the Empire.<ref name="COE" />

===Imperial encounters===
{{Quote|Wise and sturdy and great chief! Agluk is not a threat! It is the Skull Ones! They came in a flash. Destroyed the village! Put the noble Duloks in chains! You will be next!»<br />«Skull Ones?»<br />«Demons! They brought fire and lightning! They destroyed rock and tree! Almost destroyed poor Agluk! They churned the ground&hellip; and woke the Griagh!|translated=1|Agluk tells Chief Chirpa about the Empire's arrival on Endor|<ref name="SOE" />}}
Circa [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="Empire">The destruction of the Dulok [[City/Legends|village]] occurs eight [[Standard month/Legends|months]] before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], according to ''[[Star Wars: Ewoks—Shadows of Endor]]''. [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] places the Battle of Endor in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].</ref> Gorneesh's tribe<ref name="blog question">{{Tumblr|subdomain=zackules|url=post/64038252368/hi-zack-i-just-got-shadows-of-endor-a-few-days|name=Zack's Underground Rocketship|text=14th October 2013}}</ref> became intimately familiar with the Galactic Empire when the village was invaded by what the tribe took to be demons&mdash;actually [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and Imperial soldiers looking for a site to build a [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield generator bunker]] that could protect their [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around the moon. These outsiders, whom the Duloks dubbed "Skull Ones," rained untold [[Destruction of the Dulok Swamp|destruction]] on the settlement and the surrounding swamp. They inadvertently awakened a beast known as the [[Griagh]], as well; it emerged from its burrow and ravaged Duloks and Imperials alike. Once the commotion died down, the Imperials enslaved the remaining Duloks and began constructing the bunker.<ref name="SOE" />

[[File:StormtroopersDuloks-EwoksShadowsOfEndor.png|thumb|right|175px|Many Duloks were taken captive after their village was ravaged by Imperial stormtroopers.]]
A Dulok named [[Agluk]] [[Dismemberment/Legends|lost]] an arm in the chaos but escaped to take refuge in a nearby [[Unidentified Endor cave|tunnel system]]. He eventually slinked to Bright Tree Village, where he pleaded with Chirpa to help his people. The Chief caged the Dulok, but the Ewoks Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka, [[Paploo/Legends|Paploo]], and Wicket W. Warrick freed him to lead them to the site of the attacks. Joined en route by [[Latara/Legends|Latara]] and Teebo, Agluk led them to the site, where they saw the Imperial [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Renz/Legends|Renz]] order the Duloks executed, since they were too recalcitrant to be useful as slaves. Agluk led the Ewoks through the tunnels he had been living in to sneak up on the invaders and mount a rescue. Yet their alliance shattered when the Ewoks tried to free [[Zrani]], a Wistie Agluk kept captive for [[Bioluminescence/Legends|illumination]]. Firing a stormtrooper [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] he had scavenged, Agluk woke the Griagh; the newly freed Wistie led the Ewoks to safety but Agluk was torn limb from limb.<ref name="SOE" />

Agluk's tale of the Skull Ones and the Griagh also prompted the shaman Logray and Paploo to consult the [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]] [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Charal]] for information on those dangers. She foretold a period of darkness and destruction for the moon, but she also tried to steal Logray's Sunstar. She [[Zombie/Legends|reanimated]] Dulok skeletons in her attack,<ref name="ZG FB" /><ref name="SOE" /> but Paploo and Logray overcame them and regained the Sunstar. En route back to their village, the pair came across a group of stormtroopers with Dulok captives just as Zrani led the Ewok foursome out from Agluk's cavern. The Ewoks [[Skirmish at the Endor shield bunker|attacked]] the Imperials, freeing the Dulok captives from their [[Stuncuffs/Legends|stun cuffs]] so they could join the fight. However, the Griagh burst. With Sunstar in hand, Zrani flew down one of the beast's gullets, killing it but dying in the process. Now armed with stormtrooper [[Rifle/Legends|rifles]], the Duloks chased the Skull Ones into the forest. However, with their swamp gone and their numbers down, Gorneesh's tribe remained in shambles for some time.<ref name="SOE" />

===New Republic era===
Eight months later,<ref name="Empire" /> during the Battle of Endor, the Ewoks' knowledge of the ways into the Imperial bunker enabled them to lead forces from the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] into the structure to bring down the Death Star's [[Deflector shield|shields]], leaving it vulnerable to attack.<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> After their victory, the Alliance made its base on the Forest Moon, and offworld visits peaked, including the [[Second Battle of Endor|Nagai invasion]] of 4 ABY, the arrival of post-battle scavengers, the establishment of tourism, and the founding of [[Salfur's Trading Post]].<ref name="EATMS" />

[[File:University_of_Sanbra_seal.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The University of Sanbra's seal]]
Endor ostensibly became a member of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], but its representative in the Senate was an [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]] from the planet [[Maya Kovel/Legends|Maya Kovel]].<ref name="EATMS" /> In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], a team of biologists from the [[University of Sanbra]], headed by Professor [[Mankuskett]], investigated the native lifeforms of the Forest Moon. Mankuskett later wrote a report from the expedition, in which he presented the first detailed description of Duloks to the galaxy at large.<ref name="COE" />

==Behind the scenes==
===''Ewoks''===
{{Quote|Ewoks represent love, loyalty, and bravery. Duloks represent everything else.|Zack Giallongo|<ref name="Blaster">{{InsiderCite|144|Blaster}}</ref>}}
The Duloks were created by writer and artist [[Joe Johnston]] for his [[1984]] storybook, ''[[The Adventures of Teebo: A Tale of Magic and Suspense]]''. The book depicts the species as a rival group to the Ewoks, closely related, but opposite in personality. The Duloks in Johnston's story perform misdeeds that the Ewok characters abhor, including kidnapping Ewok children, threatening to eat them, and making clothing from Ewok furs.<ref name="TAOT" />

During development for the [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']] animated series, story editor [[Paul Dini]] adapted Johnston's creations for Saturday morning. Because the leader of the Duloks had died in Johnston's story, Dini created Gorneesh, Umwak, and Urgah to be the Dulok leaders for the show. Dini envisioned the Duloks as descended from a common ancestor as the Ewoks, and as sharing the Ewoks' love of the trees, albeit in the swamps instead of the forest. However, over generations, they developed into evil creatures and worshippers of the Night Spirit, making them the opposite of the good-doing Ewoks.<ref name="Starlog">{{Starlog|Yearbook Vol. 3|Saturday Morning "Star Wars"}}</ref> Dini and the other writers tamed the Duloks from their description in the Johnston storybook, making them more comical.<ref name="TAOT" /><ref name="THV" /><ref name="WW" />

[[File:Ewoks-promo.jpg|thumb|250px|Promotional image for the ''Ewoks'' series, where certain episodes with Duloks were considered by writers as the best]]
''Ewoks'' first aired in [[1985]].<ref name="SWCEL" /> Members of the species appear in the opening credits of each episode, but they feature in 8 of the 13 episodes of the first season and 3 of the 22 of the second.<ref name="SWETV">[[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']]</ref> Later writers have identified Dulok-centered episodes to be among the series' best. For example, [[Jon Bradley Snyder]] singles out "[[Asha (episode)|Asha]]" as a standout from the first season, "[[Wicket's Wagon]]" as one of the best animated outings, and "[[Rampage of the Phlogs]]" as one of the funniest thanks to a scene in which King Gorneesh has to change the diaper of a baby Phlog.<ref name="SWCEL" /> [[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]] and [[Robin Pronovost]] point to the episodes "[[The Tree of Light]]," "Wicket's Wagon," and "Asha" as the most representative of the Dulok species.<ref name="COE" />

Lucasfilm repackaged several episodes of the animated series as the feature-length films [[The Haunted Village (film)|''The Haunted Village'']] and ''[[Tales from the Endor Woods]]'' in [[2004]].<ref name="THV-DVD">[[The Haunted Village (film)|''The Haunted Village'']] (film) {{C|Compilation of "[[The Haunted Village]]," "[[The Cries of the Trees]]," "[[Rampage of the Phlogs]]," and "[[Sunstar vs. Shadowstone]]"}}</ref><ref name="TftEW-DVD">''[[Tales from the Endor Woods]]'' {{C|Compilation of "[[Wicket's Wagon]]," "[[The Travelling Jindas]]," "[[To Save Deej]]," and "[[Asha (episode)|Asha]]"}}</ref>

==Adaptations==
A variety of tie-in items were released during the run of ''Star Wars: Ewoks,'' including Dulok action figures from [[Kenner Products|Kenner]]<ref name="toy" /><ref name="Star Wars: The Action Figure Archive">''[[Star Wars: The Action Figure Archive]]''</ref> and storybook adaptations. Three Dulok-themed books were released: ''[[The Red Ghost: An Ewok Adventure]]'' from [[Random House]] in [[1986]], based on the episode "Asha,"<ref name="A" /><ref name="TRG" /> and [[The Haunted Village (book)|''The Haunted Village'']] and [[Wicket's Wagon (book)|''Wicket's Wagon'']] from [[Dragon Picture Books]] in [[1987]], based on the episodes of the same name.<ref name="THV" /><ref name="WW" /><ref name="THVb" /><ref name="WWb" /> While ''The Red Ghost'' includes all-new artwork,<ref name="TRG" /> the Dragon volumes use images taken directly from the cartoons. The Dragon volumes misspell the species' name as ''Dulock''.<ref name="THVb" /><ref name="WWb" />

[[File:Ewoks_on_ice.jpg|thumb|left|230px|Duloks appeared in "The Ewoks and the Magic Sunberries," a short ice-skating segment, in 1986.]]
A 1985 television advertisement for Kenner's ''Ewoks'' toys prominently features the Dulok characters that were sold as part of the line. Gorneesh Urgah, Umwak, and two Dulok scouts hold the Ewok shaman, Logray, captive in a wooden cage. The Ewoks assault the Duloks' position with the Ewok battle wagon, however, prompting the Dulok scouts to flee. Umwak defends the Duloks with two magic spells: the first animates a tree to fight alongside the Duloks, but the obstacle is felled by the wagon's battering ram. Umwak then creates a rift in the earth with a magical [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquake]], which separates the Duloks from the Ewoks. Nevertheless, the battle wagon's front ramp drops, and the Ewoks traverse the ravine to save their captured shaman.<ref name="Ewoks commercial">{{SWArchive|url=video/view/001087.html|text=1985 Kenner Star Wars Ewoks Action Figure Commercial|nobackup=1}}</ref>

Meanwhile, the [[Wikipedia:Spain|Spanish]] art company [[Beaumont Studios]] featured Gorneesh and his Duloks in five short scenarios released in 1986 for its ''[[MyComyc]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]]. The stories went unnoticed in the United States until [[2013]], when [[Dark Horse Comics]] Vice President of Publishing [[Randy Stradley]] explored the possibility of republishing them in one of his company's [[Star Wars Omnibus]] titles. However, staff at [[Lucasfilm]] were unable to find proof that the comics had been licensed, although there was circumstantial evidence. Thus, the ''MyComyc'' stories' status is ambiguous within [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]].<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/droids-and-ewoks-return-spains-lost-star-wars-comic-strips|text=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost ''Star Wars'' Comic Strips|int=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost Star Wars Comic Strips|nolive=1}}</ref>

In 1986, Dulok characters took to the ice as part of "[[The Ewoks and the Magic Sunberries]]," a short, live-action ice-skating segment that toured with the Ice Capades.<ref name="AGP blog 35">{{Blog|abelgpena|35|Ewoks at the Ice Capades}}</ref>

===Later sources===
[[File:Galaxies_Dulok_concept_art.jpg|thumb|right|255px|The design team of ''Star Wars Galaxies'' chose to adapt the Duloks of ''Star Wars Ewoks'' into more intimidating opponents.]]
The online computer game ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' allowed players to visit three Dulok villages and fight Dulok adversaries; visiting a Dulok village granted the player a special badge.<ref name="GAL" /><ref name="SWGCG" /><ref name="SWGTTE" /> The game's design team used the Dulok characters from ''Star Wars Ewoks'' as a basis for their own designs but tried to depict the species as fiercer and more menacing in appearance for the game.<ref name="FPTP" />

The article "Castaways of Endor," published in [[2008]] on [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]], describes heretofore unknown aspects of Dulok biology and culture.<ref name="COE" /> Robin Pronovost wrote most of the article's section on Duloks.<ref name="forums">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29533288|board=Literature|thread=Castaways of Endor sees the light of day|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan_Wallace]]|date=2008-12-02|time=10:17 AM}}</ref> An earlier version of "Castaways of Endor," slated to appear in ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine, included gaming statistics for use with the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]].<ref name="DW blog 120">{{Blog|danwallace|120|'Castaways of Endor,' New Article on StarWars.com}}</ref> This material, later released by Dan Wallace on the web, claims that Duloks speak [[Ewokese/Legends|Ewokese]]. In game terms, they are weaker, less perceptive, and less likable than most species, yet healthier. Their shamanism is likened to Ewok shamanism and Gupin magic, all three of which are described as manifestations of the Force that use different totemic foci.<ref name="COE cuts">{{WebCite|url=https://sites.google.com/site/danwall88/%22castawaysofendor%22:gamingstats|text="Castaways of Endor": Cut gaming stats|author=[[Daniel Wallace]]|archivedate=20150922060300}}</ref>

Also cut were adventure ideas involving the species. In one, a band of Duloks supplies captives to [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] slavers. Their activities threaten to wipe out Endor's Wisties, and the player characters must decide whether to step in and risk angering the Duloks and Hutts. Another scenario has a group of Duloks besieging the Gupins after a bad trade deal. The heroes have the opportunity to intervene in the dispute or to take advantage of the distraction to steal the [[Force artifact/Legends|Force artifact]] inside the Gupins' [[Juniper Chest]].<ref name="COE cuts" />

Author and artist [[Zack Giallongo]], a fan of the ''Ewoks'' cartoon, lamented the fact that more material did not address the Ewok&ndash;Dulok rivalry; he thus incorporated the Duloks into the comic book he wrote and illustrated for Dark Horse Comics, ''[[Star Wars: Ewoks—Shadows of Endor]]'', published in 2013.<ref name="Blaster" /> In the story, he attempted to return to Johnston's darker characterization of the species from their first storybook appearance.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.newsarama.com/18619-from-a-galaxy-far-away-6-yub-nub-ewoks-get-own-star-wars-comic-series.html|text=From a Galaxy Far Away 6: YUB NUB! EWOKS Get Own STAR WARS Comic Series|author=Chris Arrant|date=2013-08-08|archivedate=20170421065945}}</ref>

===Inconsistencies===
Sources disagree about the degree of familial closeness between Duloks and Ewoks. The article "Castaways of Endor" says the two species are "closely related,"<ref name="COE" /> while ''The Adventures of Teebo,'' the earliest source, calls the species "distant relatives,"<ref name="TAOT" /> a description echoed by the ''Star Wars Encyclopedia''<ref name="SWE 83" /> and ''The Essential Guide to Alien Species''.<ref name="EGAS" /> The storybook ''The Red Ghost'' instead uses the term ''cousins'' to describe the relationship,<ref name="TRG" /> terminology also used in ''The Essential Guide to Characters,''<ref name="EGC" /> the ''[[CorSec Database A-G]]'',<ref name="CSDB" /> and ''[[From Pencil to Pixel: The Art of Star Wars Galaxies]]''.<ref name="FPTP" /> Finally, both the "Endor" entry in the [[Databank (original)|original Databank]]<ref name="DB Endor" /> and the article "A Star Wars CELibration" call them "distant cousins."<ref name="SWCEL" />
